stories.title: The ML Flip
stories.subtitle: Traditional CS writes programs. ML makes the computer write them for you.
stories.intro: Traditional CS takes an input, processes it, and gives you an output. ML flips it — you have the input AND the output, and the computer figures out the processing program. That one flip changes everything about how you think about computation.

nodes.label: The Flip
nodes.content: Input → Program → Output is traditional CS. Input + Output → Program is ML. The computer writes the program. Tom Mitchell's definition: performance improving on a Task with Experience.

nodes.label: Supervised: you have the answers
nodes.content: Someone already labeled the data. The computer learns the pattern between input and label. Three flavors depending on what the label looks like.

nodes.label: Regression: the answer is a number
nodes.content: Predict house prices. Predict temperature. The output is continuous — any real number.

nodes.label: Binary classification: yes or no
nodes.content: Spam or not spam. Tumor or not tumor. The output is one of two things.

nodes.label: Multiclass: pick one from many
nodes.content: What digit is this? What breed is this dog? The output is one of N categories.

nodes.label: Unsupervised: no answers, find structure
nodes.content: Nobody labeled anything. The computer finds patterns on its own. Clustering, dimensionality reduction, density estimation.

nodes.label: Reinforcement Learning: learn by doing
nodes.content: No labels, but there's a reward signal. Take actions, get rewards, learn what works. Games, robotics, self-driving.
